what: On first open, a ruler (long ticks only at start, middle and end) lies at the bottom of the panel covering the screen, and the big year number above it counts up one year at a time over 2 seconds with circ.inOut while sliding from the ruler’s left end to its right end with the same 2-second power2.inOut. When counting finishes, the panel lifts away in .8 seconds power1.in and fx:done fires — the hero of an anniversary page that runs back from the founding year to this year

options.look: With grid, a 1px --kf-surface grid on the background (cell --fx-cell, default 55px)
options.--fx-ticks · --fx-mid: Tick count and center long tick position — default 19 ticks·52.63% (phone 10 ticks·50%)
options.[data-fx-part=track]: Ruler line — keep the count inside
options.[data-fx-part=mark]: Center logo (optional) — drop in a Lottie or image

use:
Logo
2006
note: A part that makes people wait — the original counts 2s and clears in .8s, holding for 2.8s. On screens passed often, shorten dur and fade. The original ruler is an image file, so the part draws the same tick layout with a css gradient.

from.where: shared.js loader (.t-fv — the year counts 2000→2020 with circ.inOut over 2s, while left 0→100% and xPercent -100 run power2.inOut 2s, and the panel lifts away in .8s power1.in). Same as the original custom.js #anniversary tl
